title: Beethoven concert for General von Stulpnagel
summary: The camp orchestra played Beethoven's Fifth for the Paris commander, who saluted Briggs, the only Black player, at the end.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: But, by, (in a while) we had the Commandant of Paris, it came up and we gave a concert. It was more or less a Beethoven festival.

And the Commandateur of Paris, his name was General Von Stulpnagel. He was the Commander of Paris. The Parisian regent. And he came up, and with all his staff officers and everything, and they were very surprised, 'cause I was about the only inkspot on the stand. (Laughter). And they were very surprised because that party, they believed that everything that was not Caucasian, of the Caucasian race, was a monkey or something else, you see. (Laughter).
You see. And when they realized different, at the end of the concert, the Aide de Camp, shook my hand. And the General saluted.
So, I felt pretty good. I said, 'Well, maybe I'll be spared.' (Laughter) It's by choice of God, I guess, that I'm here.
